title: Nobody glides faster than he can skate: speed above your top is shed in half a second, and an empty sprint bar must refill a quarter before the next sprint
pillar: P2 the pass is the fastest thing on the ice; P5 every key has its moment (the bar is the sprint's cost)
hypothesis: Two leaks of the owner's own speed rulings, one law. (1) thirdjam sheds speed above a skater's top only by the glide (0.147 m/s2), so a skater who takes the puck at 12.65 m/s carries it at 12.6 for seconds, not at the carrier's 10.12 (probe -which=speed: 12.57 m/s half a second after the pick-up): R-0041's 'skater with puck will need slight speed reduction ... to incentivize passing' holds from a standing start and leaks in play, where most pucks are won at speed. (2) The sprint outlives its bar twice over: by the glide (PLAY 12), and because a held sprint key on an empty bar sprints again every other frame (the gym's carrier sprints 290 of 401 frames on a 180-frame bar; found this round), so for a hand that holds Shift the bar is no cost at all. The change: speed above the skater's own full-stick top in his present state is shed at 4 m/s2 (sprint to cruise in 28 frames; a pick-up at full speed is at carrying pace in 38), and a sprint that is not running starts only on a quarter of the bar (0.75 s of sprint, 1.5 s to earn). Easing the stick glides as before (probe: unchanged). Everybody's law, bots too. Expected: the carrier is caught at the designed 2.5 m/s, so the pass is worth more to the hand (T3: taking the pass away should cost) and a carry may end sooner; the sprint becomes a spend (its share of play time falls; taking it away costs less or more, to be seen); the human's mean speed falls a little.
tempo: the sprint's speed after its bar: 14.55 m/s for many seconds becomes 12.65 within 28 frames. A carrier's speed after a pick-up at 12.65 m/s: 12.57 at 30 frames becomes 10.57 (10.12 by 38). No top speed, acceleration, stop or turn moves (gym: the skate and stop probes are equal; the chase probes move by 2-4 frames because the carrier no longer starts above his top).

why: The sprint became a spend that matters and nothing aimed elsewhere broke. For the planning hand at pro, taking the sprint away now costs 11.7 points (91.7 against 80.0 %); before the change it cost 1.6 (78.3 against 76.7). The pass turned from a cost to a gain for that hand: without it 83.3 against 91.7 % (before: 86.7 against 78.3), each figure +-7, so the sign is a lead and not yet a result (the matrix reads it paired). Wins, paired: planning hand at pro regular +13.3 +-6.5 (78.3 to 91.7), novice +8.3 +-9.9, good -1.7 +-2.9; at all-star regular -11.7 +-8.6 (63.3 to 51.7: pro and all-star move apart, which is the direction P6 wants and one and a half standard errors); thirdjam's hands at pro 0.0 / +10.0 +-6.6 / +8.3 +-7.6 (regular / novice / good), all-star +8.3 +-9.0. The human's mean speed 9.65 to 9.50 m/s; a carry and its losses unchanged (0.73 to 0.71 s, 40.5 to 38.1 %). The regular planning hand at pro is now above T8's band (60-80 %): the level table's work (round 3), as after E01b.
owner_line: Shift is a spend now: when the bar is empty you are back at skating pace within half a second, and it must fill a quarter before it answers again. And when you pick the puck up at full speed you feel yourself slow to carrying pace: a man chasing you will catch you, so move it.
notes: Found while building it: in thirdjam a held sprint key on an empty bar sprints again every other frame, so the bar never ends a held sprint (gym: 290 sprint frames of 401 on a 180-frame bar). PLAY 12 saw the speed outlive the bar and put it down to the glide alone. Probe: rinklab-thirdlife probe -which=speed. The "sprint share of play time" and every other figure are in the JSON. Measured with the planning hand of epoch k8-2 (before the hand's press timing was repaired). READ WITH CARE (added after the mid-round matrix): read through the hand before its repair (epoch k8-2). "The sprint now costs 11.7 points to lose" did not survive the repaired hand (+6.7 +-6.2 without it at 60 seeds) and is not a finding; neither is the pass's sign. What stands: the probe (14.55 m/s to 12.65 within 28 frames of the bar; a pick-up at 12.65 m/s at 10.57 after 30 frames), the held-key flicker found in thirdjam, and that no cell broke.
